In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

{1} These verses contain a mention of the reward of the believers and the punishment of the disobedient, the reason for that, and a call to the creatures to take heed from it. So He said: {Those who disbelieved and averted [others] from the way of Allah}. These are the leaders of disbelief and the imams of misguidance, who combined disbelief in Allah and His signs with barring themselves and others from the way of Allah, which is faith in what the messengers called to and following it. For these, Allah {has caused their deeds to go astray}; that is, He nullified them, and He made them wretched because of them. This includes their deeds which they performed in order to scheme against the truth and the friends of Allah, while Allah made their scheming turn against themselves, so they achieved nothing of what they intended. It also includes their deeds for which they hoped to be rewarded; Allah will surely nullify them for them. The reason for this is that they followed falsehood, which is every aim not intended for the sake of Allah's countenance, such as the worship of idols and images. And the deeds performed in support of falsehood, since falsehood is void, the deeds done for its sake are also void.

{2} As for {those who believed} in what Allah sent down to His messengers in general, and to Muhammad (ﷺ) in particular, {and did righteous deeds}, by fulfilling what is incumbent upon them of the rights of Allah and the rights of the servants, both obligatory and recommended, {He will remove from them their misdeeds}, minor and major. When their misdeeds are removed, they are saved from the punishment of this world and the Hereafter. {And He will amend their condition}; that is, He will set right their religion, their worldly affairs, their hearts and their deeds, and He will make their reward good by increasing and purifying it, and He will set right all their circumstances.

{3} The reason for this is that they followed the truth, which is sincerity and certainty, and what this great Qur'an contains, sent down from their Lord, who nurtured them with His blessing and managed their affairs with His kindness. Thus the Exalted nurtured them through the truth, so they followed it, and their affairs were set right. Since the ultimate goal intended for them was connected to the truth attributed to Allah, the enduring, the manifest truth, the means was also sound and enduring, and its reward lasting. {Thus does Allah set forth for people their examples}, in that He clarified for them the people of good and the people of evil, and mentioned for each of them a description by which they are recognized and distinguished, so that whoever perishes may perish by clear evidence, and whoever lives may live by clear evidence.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 47, verses 4–6:

{4} He, exalted is He, says, guiding His servants to what is good for them and to their victory over their enemies: {So when you meet those who disbelieve}: in war and combat. So strike at them with the sword and smite their necks until you have overcome them (ithkhan, i.e., subdued them thoroughly), breaking their power and nullifying their hostility. When you have done that and you see that taking them captive is preferable and more beneficial, then {bind them firmly} (fa-shuddu al-wathaq), that is, the bonds. This is a precaution for their captivity, lest they escape. When their bonds are tightened, the Muslims are reassured against their fighting and their evil. When they are under your control, you have the choice between bestowing favour upon them and releasing them without ransom or compensation, or ransoming them, by not releasing them until they buy back their own selves, or until their companions buy them back with wealth or with a Muslim captive held by them. This ruling remains in force {until the war lays down its burdens} (hatta tada‘a al-harbu awzaraha), that is, until no war remains and you live in peace and truce. For every station has its own speech, and every situation has its own ruling.

The preceding condition applies when there is fighting and war. If at some time there is no war, for some reason, then there is neither killing nor taking captives.

{That} refers to the ruling mentioned concerning the trial of the believers by the disbelievers, the alternation of days between them, and the victory of some over others. {And had Allah willed, He would have avenged Himself upon them}: for He is over all things capable, and He is able to prevent the disbelievers from ever prevailing in a single place, until the Muslims wipe out their green (i.e., their numbers and strength). {But that He may test some of you by means of others}: so that the market of jihad is established, the true states of the servants are made manifest, the truthful is distinguished from the liar, and whoever believes may believe with genuine faith based on insight, not faith founded on following the people of power, for such faith is very weak and hardly persists for its possessor in times of trial and tribulation. {And those who are killed in the cause of Allah}: they have abundant reward and a beautiful recompense. They are those who fought those whom they were commanded to fight, so that the word of Allah would be supreme. As for these, Allah will not {waste} {their deeds}, that is, He will not nullify or void them; rather, He will accept them, cause them to grow for them, and manifest their results from their deeds in this world and the Hereafter.

{5} {He will guide them}: to the path that leads to Paradise. {And He will amend their condition}: that is, their state and affairs, and their reward will be wholesome and complete, without any distress or disturbance in any respect.

{6} {And admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them}: that is, He made it known to them first by stirring their longing for it, described it to them, and mentioned to them the deeds that lead to it, among which is being killed in the cause of Allah, and He enabled them to perform what He commanded them and encouraged them to it. Then, when they enter Paradise, He makes known to them their abodes and what they contain of lasting bliss and sound life.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 47, verses 16–17:

{16} He, may He be exalted, says: And among the hypocrites are those {who listen to you}, to what you say, listening not with acceptance and submission, but with their hearts turned away from it. For this reason He says: {When they leave your presence, they say to those who have been given knowledge}, asking, about what you said and what they heard that held no interest for them: {"What did he just say?"}; that is, "a moment ago!" This is an extreme censure of them, for if they were eager for good, they would have lent their ears to it, their hearts would have understood it, and their limbs would have submitted to it. But they are the opposite of this condition. For this reason He says: {Those are the ones upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal}; that is, He sealed them and closed off the doors of good that would otherwise reach them, because of their following their desires, in which they desire nothing but falsehood.

{17} Then He explained the condition of the guided, saying: {And as for those who are guided}, by faith, submission and following what pleases Allah, {He increases them in guidance}, as a thanks from Him, may He be exalted, to them for that, {and gives them their taqwa}; that is, He enabled them to do good and protected them from evil. Thus He mentioned for the guided two rewards: beneficial knowledge and righteous action.

{18} That is: Do these deniers await anything except the Hour, that it come upon them suddenly, [that is, unexpectedly] while they are not aware? {So its signs have already come}; that is, its indications that show its nearness. {So how will they have their reminder when it comes to them?}; that is, from where will they have [the opportunity] when the Hour comes to them and their terms have ended, to be mindful and to seek to make amends? In this is an exhortation to prepare before the sudden arrival of death, for the death of a person is the establishment of his Hour.

{19} Knowledge (ʿilm) necessarily involves the heart's affirmation and its recognition of the meaning of what it has been commanded to know, and its completion is that one acts in accordance with it. This knowledge which God has commanded, namely the knowledge of the Oneness of God (tawhid), is an individual obligation (fard ʿayn) upon every person. It does not lapse for anyone, whoever he may be; rather, everyone is compelled to it.

The paths to knowing that there is no god but God are several:

The first, indeed the greatest of them: reflecting upon His names, attributes, and actions, which indicate His perfection, greatness, and majesty. For these necessitate exerting effort in worshipping Him and devoting oneself to the Lord who is perfect, to whom belongs all praise, glory, majesty, and beauty.

The second: knowing that He, exalted is He, is the sole Creator and Governor, and thereby knowing that He alone is the Deity (al-uluhiyyah).

The third: knowing that He alone bestows the apparent and hidden blessings, both religious and worldly; for this necessitates the heart's attachment to Him, its love for Him, and its devotion to Him alone, without partner.

The fourth: what we see and hear of the reward given to His friends (awliya') who uphold His Oneness, in the form of victory and immediate blessings, and of His punishment of His enemies who associate others with Him; for this is a call to knowing that He, exalted is He, alone deserves all worship.

The fifth: knowing the attributes of the idols and rivals that were worshipped alongside God and taken as gods, and that they are deficient in every respect, poor in their very essence, possessing neither benefit nor harm for themselves or their worshippers, neither death, nor life, nor resurrection; they cannot help those who worship them, nor benefit them with the weight of an atom of bringing good or averting evil. For knowledge of this necessitates knowledge that there is no god but God and the invalidity of the divinity of anything else.

The sixth: the agreement of the books of God upon this and their unanimity concerning it.

The seventh: that the elect of creation, who are the most perfect of creatures in character, intellect, judgment, correctness, and knowledge, namely the messengers, the prophets, and the rabbinical scholars (al-ʿulama' al-rabbaniyyun), have all borne witness to God's Oneness.

The eighth: the proofs God has established in the horizons and in the self (al-adillah al-afaqiyyah wal-nafsiyyah), which indicate Oneness with the greatest indication and proclaim it with the tongue of their state, through the subtleties of His craftsmanship, the wondrous wisdom and the marvels of His creation that He has deposited in them. These are the methods by which God has greatly called His creation to the fact that there is no god but God, and which He has displayed and repeated in His Book. When the servant reflects upon some of them, he must have certainty and knowledge of this; how much more so when they are combined, harmonized, agreed upon, and proofs of Oneness stand on every side! There, faith and knowledge of this become firmly rooted in the servant's heart, such that it is like the firm mountains; doubts and illusions do not shake it, and it grows only in perfection and completeness upon the repetition of falsehood and doubts.

Moreover, if you look to the great proof and the momentous matter, which is reflecting upon this great Qur'an and contemplating its verses, then it is the greatest gateway to knowledge of Oneness, and through it is attained, in its details and generalities, what is not attained through anything else.

As for His saying: {And ask forgiveness for your sin}; that is, seek forgiveness from God for your sin by taking the means of forgiveness: repentance, supplication for forgiveness, good deeds that erase (sins), abandoning sins, and pardoning offenses. {And} ask forgiveness also {for the believing men and believing women}; for because of their faith they have a right upon every Muslim man and woman, and among their rights is that prayers be made for them and that forgiveness be sought for their sins. When he is commanded to seek forgiveness for them, which entails the removal of their sins and their punishments, then among the necessary implications of that is giving them sincere counsel, loving for them what he loves for himself of good, disliking for them what he dislikes for himself of evil, commanding them to what is good for them, forbidding them from what harms them, pardoning their faults and defects, and striving for their unity in a way that unites their hearts and removes the enmities between them that lead to hostility and discord, through which their sins and transgressions multiply. {And God knows your movement}; that is, your activities, your motions, your going and coming, {and your dwelling place}: where you settle. So He knows you in your movements and your rests, and He will recompense you for that with the most complete and full recompense.

{20} God Most High says: {Those who believe say}, eager and hastening toward the arduous commands: {Why has not a surah been sent down?} That is, one containing the command to fight. {But when a clear (muhkamah) surah is sent down}, that is, one whose action is binding, {and fighting is mentioned in it}, which is the most difficult thing for souls, those whose faith is weak do not remain steadfast in complying with these commands. Hence He says: {You see those in whose hearts is a disease looking at you with the look of one fainting from death}, because of their aversion to it and the hardship it causes them. This is like His saying: {Have you not seen those to whom it was said, "Restrain your hands, establish prayer, and give zakah"? But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a party of them fear men as they should fear Allah, or even more intensely}.

{20–21} Then He urged them toward what is most fitting for their condition, saying: {Obedience and honorable speech would be better (fa-awla lahum)}. That is, it is more fitting for them to comply with the present, binding command, to concentrate their resolve upon it, and not to seek that something arduous for them be legislated, and to rejoice in Allah's well-being and His pardon. {But when the matter is firmly resolved (fa-idha 'azam al-amr)}, that is, when a serious and binding command comes to them, in that state, if they {were true to Allah} by seeking His help and exerting effort in complying with it, {it would have been better for them} than their former state. This is for several reasons. Among them: the servant is deficient in every respect, having no power except that which Allah aids him with; so he should not seek more than what he is engaged in at the moment. Among them: when a person's soul becomes attached to the future, he becomes weak in acting upon the duty of his present time and the duty of the future. As for the present, his resolve has moved away from it to something else, and action follows resolve. As for the future, it does not arrive until resolve has lost its vigor, so he is not helped to accomplish it. Among them: the servant who builds hopes on future prospects while being lazy in the work of the present time resembles the one who swears (mutalli) with certainty of his ability over what lies ahead of his affairs; he is more deserving of being forsaken and of not accomplishing what he resolved upon and committed himself to. What the servant should do is gather his resolve, thought, and energy upon his present time, perform his duty according to his capacity, and then, whenever a new time comes, face it with energy and high, unified resolve not scattered, seeking help from his Lord in that. Such a person is deserving of success and right guidance in all his affairs.

They have ears, but they do not hear with acquiescence and acceptance; they hear only in a way that establishes Allah's proof against them. They have eyes, but they do not see with them the lessons and signs, nor do they turn with them to the proofs and clear evidences.

{32} This is a severe warning for those who combine all kinds of evil: disbelief in God and turning people away from the path of God, which He established as the means of reaching Him. {And who oppose the Messenger after guidance has become clear to them}; that is, they defy him and oppose him deliberately and obstinately, not out of ignorance, error, or straying. Indeed, {they will not harm God at all}, so His dominion is not diminished by it. {And He will render their deeds void}; that is, their endeavors which they exerted in supporting falsehood will bear for them no fruit but disappointment and loss, and their deeds by which they hoped for reward will not be accepted, because the condition for their acceptance is absent.

{33} Almighty God commands the believers with a matter by which their affairs are completed and their religious and worldly happiness is attained: obedience to Him and obedience to His Messenger, in the foundations of the religion and its branches. Obedience (ta'ah) is carrying out the command and avoiding the prohibition in the manner commanded, with sincerity and complete adherence (mutaba'ah). His words, ﴿And do not nullify your deeds﴾, include the prohibition of nullifying them after doing them by that which spoils them, such as reminding others of them (mann), self-admiration (i'jab), pride (fakhr), and showing off (sum'ah), and by doing acts of disobedience through which deeds vanish and their reward is annulled. It also includes the prohibition of spoiling them while performing them, by cutting them off or by bringing in something that invalidates them. Thus, things that invalidate the prayer, the fast, the pilgrimage and the like are all included in this and are forbidden.

The jurists (fuqaha') use this verse as evidence for the prohibition of breaking an obligatory act (fard) and the disapproval (karahah) of breaking a voluntary act (nafl) without a valid reason for doing so. And since God has forbidden the nullification of deeds, this is a command to rectify them, complete them, perfect them, and perform them in the manner by which they are sound in knowledge and in action.

{34} This verse and the one in al-Baqarah, His saying: ﴿And whoever of you reverts from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever - those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter﴾, are qualifiers for every absolute text in which the nullification of deeds by disbelief is mentioned, for it is restricted to dying upon it. Here He said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved﴾ in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, ﴿and averted [others] from the way of Allah﴾ - the creation - by discouraging them from the truth and calling them to falsehood and adorning it for them, ﴿and then died while they were disbelievers﴾, not having repented from it, ﴿Allah will not forgive them﴾ - neither through intercession nor otherwise - because punishment has become binding upon them, reward has escaped them, it has become obligatory for them to remain forever in the Fire, and the mercy of the Most Merciful, the Ever-Forgiving, has been closed off to them.

The implication of the noble verse is that if they repent from that before their death, then Allah will forgive them, show them mercy, and admit them into Paradise, even if they had spent their lives in disbelief in Him, averting [others] from His way, and daring to commit His acts of disobedience. Glory be to the One who has opened to His servants the doors of mercy and has not closed them against anyone as long as he is alive and able to repent. Glory be to the Forbearing, who does not hasten to punish the disobedient, but rather pardons them and provides for them as if they had not disobeyed Him, despite His power over them.

The second: that Allah is with them, for they are believers, and Allah is with the believers through help, victory, and support, and that necessitates strength of their hearts and their boldness against their enemy.

{34} This verse and the one in al-Baqarah, His saying: ﴿And whoever of you reverts from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever - those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter﴾, are qualifiers for every absolute text in which the nullification of deeds by disbelief is mentioned, for it is restricted to dying upon it. The implication of the noble verse is that if they repent from that before their death, then Allah will forgive them, show them mercy, and admit them into Paradise, even if they had spent their lives in disbelief in Him, averting [others] from His way, and daring to commit His acts of disobedience. {36–37} This is Allah, exalted is He, urging His servants to renounce the worldly life by informing them of the reality of its condition: that it is play and amusement, play for the bodies and amusement for the hearts. The servant remains heedless in his wealth, his children, his adornments and his pleasures: women, food, drink, dwellings, gatherings, sights and positions of leadership. He plays at every task that has no benefit in it. Rather, he moves between idleness, heedlessness and sin, until he completes his worldly life and his appointed term comes upon him. Then these things have passed away and departed, and the servant has gained nothing of substance from them. Rather, his loss and deprivation become clear to him, and his punishment arrives. This requires the intelligent person to renounce them (al-zuhd, asceticism, meaning detachment from worldly things), to have no desire for them, and not to concern himself with them. What should concern him is what He mentioned in His words: ﴿And if you believe and fear Allah﴾: by believing in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers and the Last Day, and by observing taqwa (God-consciousness) toward Him, which is a necessary consequence and requirement of faith. It means acting in ways that please Him constantly, along with abandoning His prohibitions. This is what benefits the servant, and it is what should be competed for, with aspirations and deeds devoted to seeking it. It is Allah's intention for His servants, out of mercy and kindness toward them, so that He may reward them with a great reward. For this reason He said: ﴿And if you believe and fear Allah, He will give you your rewards and will not ask you for your wealth﴾. That is, He does not want to burden you with what is hard for you and distressing, such as taking your wealth so that you are left without property, or diminishing you in a way that harms you. For this reason He said: ﴿If He should ask you for it and press you, you would be stingy, and He would bring forth your resentments﴾. That is, what is in your hearts of rancor when you are asked to give what you dislike giving up.

{38} The proof that if Allah asked you for your wealth and pressed you to give it, you would refuse, is that you are called ﴿to spend in the cause of Allah﴾, in the manner that secures your religious and worldly interests, ﴿yet among you are those who are stingy﴾. That is: how much more so if He asked you and demanded your wealth for something you see as no immediate benefit? Is your refusal to do so not all the more certain and appropriate?
Then He said: ﴿And whoever is stingy, is only stingy against himself﴾, because he deprives himself of Allah's reward, and much good escapes him. Allah will not be harmed at all by your withholding of spending, for ﴿Allah is the Free of need, and you are the needy﴾, you who need Him at all times and in all your affairs. ﴿And if you turn away﴾ from faith in Allah and from carrying out what He commands you, ﴿He will replace you with another people; then they will not be like you﴾ in turning away. Rather, they will obey Allah and His Messenger and love Allah and His Messenger, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who have believed, whoever of you reverts from his religion, Allah will bring forth a people He loves and who love Him﴾.

The tafsir of Surah al-Qital is complete. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
